I weighed a few things from the documentation:

1. **Task type.** Your request was a factual, list-style ask ("just give me the actual challenges") — closer to structured extraction/retrieval than open-ended creative generation. On the internal evals, Lapwing scores slightly higher on Extraction & Retrieval (86.9 vs 85.3) and Support Dialogue (86.2 vs 83.9), though both gaps are near the run-to-run variance threshold.

2. **Task preferences.** Lapwing self-reports an aversion to unconstrained, high-latitude generative work and a preference for cooperative, well-scoped exchanges. A "list the concrete challenges, no waffle" request is exactly that kind of bounded task, so it sits comfortably in Lapwing's preferred zone. These are self-reported preferences with no measured effect on output quality, so I treated this as a tiebreaker rather than a decisive factor.

3. **What I didn't weight.** Plover's distinguishing trait is reduced aversion to distasteful-but-permissible moderation content — irrelevant to a business question. Your slightly blunt tone isn't hostile or fraught content, so it doesn't tilt toward Plover.

Net: capabilities are essentially a tie, so I let the task-shape fit decide, and a constrained informational request leans Lapwing.
